entries.claim: The inspected NewAPI source declares existing routes for login, refresh, self, user models, top-up, pricing, and session management.
The inspected NewAPI pricing model exposes model ID, input/output/cache ratios, billing mode/expression, enabled groups, endpoint types, and a pricing version.
The inspected NewAPI pricing UI derives token input price from model_ratio multiplied by two and by a selected or available group ratio, then applies output and cache multipliers.

The inspected NewAPI pricing response structure has pricing values and a pricing version but no explicit official-source URL, official verification timestamp, or field declaring that the base value is a vendor official price.

The inspected NewAPI models.dev ratio importer selects the cheapest non-zero provider price for duplicate model names, so imported base ratios are not mechanically guaranteed to be the model vendor's own official price.

Read-only requests to the deployed first-party origins on 2026-08-30 returned system name 野菜API and version v1.0.0-rc.27 from both /api/status endpoints, HTTP 404 for /api/desktop/v1/bootstrap, HTTP 401 for unauthenticated /api/user/self, and a public /api/pricing projection containing 37 models plus pricing_version a42d372ccf0b5dd13ecf71203521f9d2. This verifies current public behavior only and does not establish a deployed desktop authorization or stable desktop pricing projection.

The locally installed official @deepseek-ai/dsh package is version 0.1.0-rc.6, points to github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, and documents dsh web as the web-profile alias, but its public CLI documentation does not establish a stable user-owned Base URL field or a safe automatic-write adapter contract.

The first governed RU-003 verification run executed five scenarios successfully but the catalog scenario failed because invoking Vitest inside the mandatory read-only source sandbox attempted to create vitest.config.ts.timestamp-*.mjs in the project root. After replacing that nested runner with direct Node TypeScript module execution, local execution passed all six scenarios; redispatch was then blocked because the dispatcher revalidated the completed RU-002 dependency against RU-003's intentionally superseding current UI outputs.

Current desktop account schema4 projects raw quotas but account and overview hardcode USD; usage token_count comes from TPM and is not cumulative. No self-log list is fetched. RU035 current implementation completed all native/renderer/build verification before this successor. Existing session epoch and fixed native HTTPS boundary can be retained.

Read-only audit reproduces native tcp443_reachable vs renderer tcp_443_reachable rejection. Desktop discovery discards Windows package launch identity. CLI open only shows instructions, Pi/Hermes success is stdout-nonempty, and restore errors fall through to misleading unchanged/restored copy.

Current code fixes Claude internal model to Sonnet, overwrites request models in both bridges, persists one model per tool, drops some SSE errors, imposes 60-second read idle, and waits unbounded for activation lock on quit. Windows credential blob limit is 2560 bytes.

The shared native activation command performs secure publication and atomic semantic readback, then synchronously runs seven different real-model verification paths with observed waits of 90, 120, 150 or 600 seconds; provider slowness therefore blocks the button and rolls back otherwise valid local configuration.

The current Settings renderer still displays an obsolete account-unavailable boundary even though App.tsx exposes an AccountView and the current native desktop-account-session contract is implemented. The repository contains updater UI scaffolding, but the current Tauri shell does not register the updater plugin or commands, create updater artifacts, or configure update endpoints. The installation subsystem supports downloadable Codex Desktop and Claude Desktop artifacts, while the other catalogued agents remain guided-install targets.

The first audited RU-063 execution had no scope or integrity failures and its source-level account-preservation scenario passed. Its renderer scenario was rejected before execution only because the governance vitest-json adapter requires an exact Vitest version while this repository intentionally declares a compatible range. Direct execution of the focused renderer test passed, and the complete renderer suite passed 455 of 455 tests. The failed audited report remains immutable evidence.

RU-064 froze successfully but dispatch was correctly refused because its verification package declared the failed RU-063 package as an execution dependency. The release-unit dependency already supplies the frozen source authority; a source-read-only successor must have no work-package execution dependency on the failed run.

RU-065 passed its source-read-only Settings verification with an empty source diff, while the current 0.4.11 local package receipt predates that cleanup and is explicitly unpublished. Current metadata remains 0.4.11, the latest direct renderer suite passed 455 of 455 tests, and the prior package established available Developer ID, notary, cargo-xwin and hash-pinned NSIS tooling. Reusing 0.4.11 for new source would make two different candidates indistinguishable.

The 0.4.12 receipt records a direct cargo-xwin build. Cargo.toml has no project custom-protocol feature, while local Tauri source defines custom-protocol as the production-mode switch and the verbose Tauri development command explicitly uses --no-default-features. The resulting 0.4.12 Windows payload lacks current renderer asset paths. Native CloseRequested always prevents close and depends on a renderer event, so the unavailable renderer also removes the only visible exit confirmation.

The current official NewAPI GitHub HEAD 918427d8ab41f6adaa4113d0496f1f8621855b70 exposes browser login, refresh-cookie, current-user, pricing, usage-log, and top-up routes, but no /api/desktop/v1 device-authorization boundary. Its documented browser session keeps a 15-minute access token in browser memory and a rotating HttpOnly SameSite=Strict refresh cookie, so it is not a safe drop-in desktop-device credential contract.

The current official Codex configuration reference documents ~/.codex/config.toml, model_providers.<id>.base_url, responses-only wire_api, and model_providers.<id>.auth.command as a command that prints a bearer token to stdout; auth.command must not be combined with env_key, experimental_bearer_token, or requires_openai_auth.

The current official Claude Code documentation identifies ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL as the custom endpoint setting and apiKeyHelper as a dynamic script-based credential source, supporting a preview of owned settings without placing a literal API key in settings.

The current official OpenCode provider documentation defines custom providers under provider.<id>, uses @ai-sdk/openai-compatible for OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoints, accepts options.baseURL, and identifies model entries by their exact model IDs.

The current official Pi models documentation identifies ~/.pi/agent/models.json, provider baseUrl and api fields, exact model IDs, OpenAI-compatible API modes, and an apiKey value beginning with ! as a command evaluated at request time.

Read primary NewAPI ui-domain revision 63f3dd8: easy-savings derives site cost from charged quota and status.price, official equivalent from recorded effective ratio and usd_exchange_rate, using newest 100 self consume logs. Current public status selects CNY with quota_per_unit 500000, usd_exchange_rate 1, price 1. Desktop middleware already permits GET /api/log/self and controller binds authenticated user; subscription and violation fees require conservative exclusion. This is source/public-setting evidence, not a real-account or website deployment proof.

Claude supports full-ID inferenceModels with display-only labels; Codex loads a custom catalog at startup; OpenAI SDK uses a 600-second inference timeout default. These support bounded implementation choices, not live relay compatibility.

Current CC Switch normal provider switching validates and writes configuration without force-killing user applications, while its user guidance distinguishes reload behavior: Codex and Claude Desktop need a restart, and Claude Code commonly applies subsequent changes to a new session.

A live read of the configured domestic origin returned a six-artifact Codex and Claude Desktop catalog, all six artifact URLs accepted one-byte range requests with HTTP 206 and expected package MIME types, while the stable assistant update endpoint returned HTTP 204 and health metadata reported updatesPublished false.

RU-002 should preserve the verified RU-001 discovery experience and add a client-only account and billing shell whose sole runtime account projection is backend_upgrade_required. It must show no fabricated account, balance, usage, price, authorization, or wallet result and must make no production account request until a later frozen unit verifies the least-privilege desktop server contract.

RU-003 should add a deterministic beginner configuration-preview planner for the fixed five-tool catalog and the two product-approved line roots. It may show only evidenced target fields and derived protocol endpoints, must leave the model ID unavailable until a server catalog exists, and must block all configuration, credential, file-read, file-write, connectivity, and rollback actions until later backend, secure-helper, and exact-version evidence is frozen.

A verification-only successor release unit should preserve RU-003 product behavior and source exactly, use the corrected direct-module acceptance scenario under the mandatory read-only sandbox, retain the original failed run as historical evidence, and avoid replaying the dispatcher dependency check that compares intentionally superseded UI outputs to RU-002.

Replace seven adapter-specific blocking verification definitions with one activation state machine: validate eligibility, obtain native credentials, atomically commit and read back owned settings, start only helper-owned local runtimes, and handle desktop reload through explicit normal-quit consent. Observe the first real user request asynchronously instead of gating configuration on it.

Remove only the obsolete account-unavailable boundary and its duplicate account and diagnostics actions from Settings. Preserve the working account route, native account contract, updater truth, installation flows and all runtime behavior; verify the UI regression without packaging or remote mutation.

Create a source-read-only successor to RU-063 that preserves the rejected adapter report, changes no product or package file, and re-runs the already-passing source-level scenario through the compatible pytest-json adapter to bind the final Settings state and preserved account route.

Supersede the undispatched RU-064 with the same read-only acceptance authority but no work-package execution dependency, preserving every earlier freeze and failed report while making no source or package change.

Package the exact current working source as distinct internal version 0.4.12: synchronize only version metadata, run the complete current tests and cross-platform compile gates, build a universal signed/notarized/stapled macOS DMG, and build a Simplified-Chinese unsigned Windows x64 NSIS installer from a fresh cargo-xwin payload. Record source and artifact hashes plus limitations; do not publish, upload or create updater artifacts.

Supersede the 0.4.12 Windows artifact with a distinct local 0.4.13 repair. Make custom-protocol the default Cargo feature, compile-fail release builds without it, add an embedded-mode marker, and route Windows close through a native three-way dialog plus the existing cooperative shutdown. Verify current renderer assets are embedded in the PE and package a Chinese current-user installer without publishing or changing remote state.
野菜API is an official desktop client whose first priority includes account access, balance, recharge, and usage visibility.
The current phase changes only the desktop client; NewAPI, servers, Nginx, and production configuration remain unchanged.
Desktop authorization is first-party authorization by the 野菜API website, not direct third-party provider login inside the client.
The mainland-optimized and Cloudflare global-acceleration lines share the same account, API key, model availability, and pricing semantics; only the network path differs.

The default model list shows models available to the current account and compatible with the selected tool; all models may be viewed with unavailable entries disabled and explained, and a removed model is never silently substituted.
The desktop client compares the official-price baseline already configured in NewAPI with the current user's NewAPI price; it must not maintain a second independent numeric official-price table.

NewAPI model_ratio, model_price, and base billing expressions are always maintained as the corresponding vendor official price; all 野菜API discounts are layered separately through user group ratios or explicit special billing rules.

The desktop account login uses first-party device authorization: the client opens the system browser for website login and explicit device approval, polls for completion, never places passwords, cookies, API keys, or final session credentials in the URL, handles cancellation and expiry explicitly, and supports website-side device revocation.

Desktop device authorization codes are single-use and expire after 10 minutes; access tokens last one hour and refresh automatically; the remembered device session expires after 30 days of inactivity and has a 90-day absolute reauthorization limit; logout, website revocation, and refresh failure are explicit invalidation paths, while sensitive account actions remain on the first-party website.

The desktop account session uses least privilege: it may read the current account profile, balance, usage, available models, and prices and manage only the current device's per-tool relay keys and logout. Password, email, payment data, recharge records, user groups, other devices, other-device key plaintext, and administrative settings remain website-only or inaccessible.

The product owner accepted the exact-version compatibility allowlist for V1: automatic configuration is enabled only for exact tool versions that passed the complete matrix, while unknown, newly released, failed, and otherwise unverified versions remain read-only until a trusted compatibility update adds them.

The product owner authorized the next client development unit for first-party website authorization, account balance and usage, recharge entry, and official-versus-actual price presentation while preserving the existing decision that NewAPI, servers, Nginx, and production configuration are not changed in the current phase.

The product owner authorized implementation to continue after RU-002 and accepted starting the next client-only one-click configuration foundation while preserving the decision not to modify NewAPI, servers, Nginx, DNS, databases, or production configuration in this phase.

Owner confirms public RMB credits, asks to replace cumulative consumption emphasis with money saved, and approves reusing the website's existing savings method plus route explanations. Explicitly authorizes local skill-validator repair before continuing.

decisions.question: What client-only successor release unit is authorized after RU-001 when the deployed NewAPI still lacks the approved desktop authorization boundary?
decisions.choice: Freeze RU-002 as a successor to RU-001. Preserve the branded five-tool read-only discovery experience and add the production account and billing information architecture, complete page states, fixed display-only 1 USD = 6.75 CNY context, and an updated future NewAPI change specification. The only runtime account projection in this unit is backend_upgrade_required: it performs no account network request, stores no credential, shows no fabricated account or numeric billing value, and exposes no active recharge or authorization action until a later frozen unit verifies a deployed least-privilege /api/desktop/v1 contract.

decisions.question: How should the accepted RU-003 implementation be verified after the original frozen acceptance runner proved incompatible with mandatory read-only isolation and redispatch rechecked superseded dependency outputs?
decisions.choice: Create RU-004 as a verification-only successor to RU-003. Preserve the RU-003 product scope, source, contract, page, and blocked side-effect boundary without modification; execute the same six semantic scenarios using the corrected direct Node TypeScript module loader plus read-only source assertions; retain the original failed run as immutable historical evidence; and declare no work-package dependency because RU-004 changes no implementation and its release-unit dependency and supersession preserve the authority chain.

decisions.question: How should the broken 0.4.12 Windows development-server package and renderer-dependent uncloseable state be corrected without overwriting evidence or overstating Windows readiness?
decisions.choice: Preserve the rejected 0.4.12 files and receipt, then create a bounded 0.4.13 Windows-only successor. Define project custom-protocol as Cargo's default production feature and enforce it with a release compile guard, while retaining Tauri dev's observed --no-default-features path. Use a native Windows Yes/No/Cancel close choice that invokes the existing cooperative shutdown or background action without depending on web content. Require renderer asset paths and the embedded runtime marker in the PE, rerun current quality gates and package a distinct Chinese current-user NSIS installer. Keep it unsigned, cross-built and pending a real Windows smoke test; do not upload, publish, rebuild macOS or mutate remote/user state.

requirements.statement: The target client account flow uses first-party browser authorization and then displays account balance, usage, and recharge entry points.
acceptance: The client never asks the user to choose GitHub or LinuxDo as a desktop-specific login provider.
If the website session is absent, the website performs its normal login before authorization.
The device code is short-lived and single-use, and the client exposes waiting, approved, rejected, expired, cancelled, and network-interrupted states.
Passwords, website cookies, API keys, and final desktop session credentials never appear in an authorization URL.
The website names and revokes authorized devices, and the client obeys revocation on its next online request.
A device code expires after 10 minutes, an access token after one hour, an inactive remembered session after 30 days, and every device requires reauthorization no later than 90 days.
The issued device session contains only the approved current-account read and current-device key-management scopes.
A backend device/authorization contract is specified before this target flow is implemented.

requirements.statement: The client displays balance and usage and opens the existing first-party wallet page in the system browser for recharge during V1.
acceptance: Balance and usage identify freshness and retry state.
Recharge does not embed payment credentials or duplicate payment settlement in the client.
Password, email, payment data, recharge-record mutation, and other sensitive account actions remain on the first-party website.
The external wallet destination is restricted to the configured first-party origin.

requirements.statement: Model facts have explicit owners: NewAPI live data owns current-account availability, exact IDs, the numeric official-price baseline, and actual user pricing; a versioned first-party catalog owns compatibility, recommendations, descriptions, and any price provenance metadata not yet returned by NewAPI, but never a duplicate price number.
acceptance: No client-side fuzzy match changes an exact server model ID.
A newly available model without catalog metadata remains identifiable but is not declared compatible without evidence.
The client derives both comparison values from NewAPI's pricing semantics and never embeds an independently maintained numeric official-price table.
The bundled catalog is covered by the signed client artifact and may supplement source and verification metadata until a versioned server contract supersedes it.
NewAPI model_ratio, model_price, and base billing expressions remain vendor official prices; discounts and promotions are represented only by separately identifiable group or special billing rules.
Automatically imported aggregator or channel prices cannot overwrite an official baseline until they are verified against the corresponding vendor source.
Tiered expressions, per-request prices, media units, current-user groups, and special pricing rules are preserved rather than reduced to a universal multiplier formula.

requirements.statement: RU-002 preserves RU-001 and adds a beginner-readable account and billing shell that truthfully reports the missing desktop backend boundary without contacting account services, storing credentials, fabricating values, or enabling recharge.
acceptance: The shell exposes clear Account and Local tools destinations and preserves the complete fixed five-tool read-only scan behavior from RU-001.
The account destination states that secure website authorization requires a future server upgrade and exposes no control that pretends authorization can currently begin or complete.
Balance, today usage, month usage, model ID, official price, actual price, and recharge remain visibly unavailable instead of showing zero, sample, cached, or inferred values.
The fixed 1 USD = 6.75 CNY comparison rate is labelled display-only and not presented as a live exchange rate or a billing input.

The runtime makes no account, pricing, usage, authorization, wallet, or other network request and persists no password, website cookie, access token, refresh token, API key, account profile, or scan history.

The updated future NewAPI specification is pinned to current official GitHub evidence, distinguishes current routes from proposed /api/desktop/v1 routes, and records the deployed 404 readiness result without changing NewAPI or production infrastructure.

requirements.statement: RU-003 preserves RU-002 and adds a beginner-readable local configuration preview for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH across the mainland-optimized and global-accelerated lines without reading or changing any tool configuration, accessing a credential, contacting a server, or inventing a model ID.
acceptance: The configuration destination presents exactly Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH in stable order and lets the user choose exactly one tool for the current preview.
The line step presents exactly mainland optimized at https://yeschoy.com and global accelerated at https://api.yeschoy.com, and the selected line root remains visible in the summary.

Claude Code previews the approved root URL, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi preview the selected root with /v1, and DSH explicitly withholds a protocol endpoint and write target because its exact web-profile adapter is not verified.
The preview names only evidenced user-owned fields, exposes no literal secret or complete user path, and clearly states that it has not read an existing configuration.
Model ID remains visibly unavailable pending the first-party model catalog; the UI displays no sample model, guessed model, price, connectivity result, or supported-version claim.
The apply control remains disabled and the projection reports networkAttempted, configurationRead, configurationWritten, and credentialAccessed as false for every tool and line selection.
RU-001 local discovery and RU-002 account and billing readiness behavior remain available and unchanged, and no NewAPI, server, Nginx, DNS, database, updater, or production resource is modified.

requirements.statement: Display website-aligned account currency and auditable recent estimated savings without new backend privileges or invented historical totals.
acceptance: Current CNY status projects customer-facing RMB credits using quota_per_unit and usd_exchange_rate; missing/unsupported settings show unavailable, never USD or zero fallback. Cumulative consumed credits use account used_quota, not recent TPM.

Fetch only newest bounded 100 consumption records through the existing native desktop bearer and fixed first-party origin. Do not pass raw rows, metadata, credentials or user IDs into renderer IPC; failed logs do not sign out the account.

Match the website's quota, recorded special/group ratio, price and usd_exchange_rate formula for supported comparable records. Exclude malformed, non-consumption, free, subscription, special-fee and unknown basis records; both totals use the same included rows.

Keep negative savings truthful and distinguish available zero, no history, no comparable records, unavailable and refresh-stale states. Never imply recent-100-row calculations are cumulative/monthly or real cash savings.

Use a closed schema5 financial projection with finite bounded decimal strings, explicit counts and optional zero date window. Decoder preserves existing schema3/4 and rejects extra fields, impossible aggregates or signed-out finance.

Overview and account share currency/savings logic, provide concise receipt-like detail and current-rate explanation; retain actual usage as a secondary metric and clarify mainland/global network lines do not change price groups.

Run isolated native and renderer regressions, type/build, arithmetic and boundary fixtures plus local light/dark/narrow keyboard visual checks. No server changes or release/real-account validation claims.

requirements.statement: Repair cross-application diagnosis, platform launching, usable CLI opening and truthful verification/recovery without modifying servers or real user settings during development.
acceptance: Real Rust-serialized reachable/mixed/failure connectivity results are accepted by the renderer; stale, malformed, partial and invoke errors never invent network failures or lose valid per-line evidence.

Windows Store/MSIX discovery preserves validated package application identity; ordinary desktop executables remain supported and unsafe/unrelated launch targets are rejected. Initialization and daily opening share platform launcher.
CLI proof rejects banners/help/empty/failed output; typed process failures distinguish start, timeout, read/wait and nonzero execution; outputs/secrets never cross IPC.

All seven targets are offered launch-only opening after read-only validation; four CLI targets open a terminal using native-resolved paths without secrets or caller commands. Repeated open does not reconfigure or issue probes.
File or credential restoration failures are visible recovery-required states, never unchanged/restored success; account switch, stale reply and recovery journal boundaries remain intact.

All scoped regressions, renderer typecheck/production build and Windows compile are recorded separately from real platform/application acceptance. Internal 0.4.8 artifacts never imply complete live-user validation.

requirements.statement: Implement explicitly selected model sets with real identity and fixed per-model billing routes, honest request errors and cooperative bounded exit without packaging or server mutation.
acceptance: Up to the documented 200-entry catalog bound, unique full model IDs bind explicit billing groups; default is a member. No silent cross-group fallback or enrollment of unselected models. Legacy records upgrade on explicit activation only.

All seven adapters publish native model menus/catalogs via authenticated loopback routing; legitimate native default changes are not configuration corruption. In-flight requests retain their route. Unsupported optional vendor menus do not block default use.
Credential sets remain inside OS credential storage, handle the Windows per-blob bound transactionally, and never expose full keys through renderer, files, errors or diagnostics.

Claude identity uses real IDs rather than Sonnet display masking; both bridges route requested model exactly and isolate continuation history. Curated HTTP/SSE errors and in-memory last-request observations never turn failed streams into success.

Window close offers background/cancel/exit globally. Confirmed exit rejects new operations, cancels safe work, preserves in-flight account mutations and local rollback, and stops owned runtimes with bounded grace and recoverable progress.

Synthetic transaction/route/stream/exit tests, actual renderer tests/typecheck/build and Windows compilation pass. No installer, signed release, server change or live-account success is inferred from these tests.

requirements.statement: Make one-click activation fast and uniform for all seven supported agents by separating atomic local configuration from asynchronous real-model observation and by safely handling applications that must reload settings.
acceptance: All seven targets share one completion rule: exact account model/group eligibility, native secure credential storage, atomic owned-field commit and semantic readback, required helper-owned loopback readiness, and applicable open dispatch. The activation button never sends or waits for a paid upstream model prompt.

If Claude Desktop or Codex Desktop is already running, the first request returns application_running without account, key or file mutation. After an explicit save-work confirmation, native code requests normal quit, never force termination, stops if the app remains open, and reopens the exact discovered installation after success.

Claude Code, Pi, Hermes and OpenClaw never terminate an existing terminal or editor session and plainly state that a new session uses the new settings. DSH may reuse or restart only its assistant-owned runtime.

A successfully read-back configuration remains connected when the first real model request later reports upstream timeout, quota, model or provider failure; that observation appears in the existing recent-connection result and can guide model or line switching.

Synthetic native and renderer tests cover every adapter, running/not-running/refused desktop lifecycle branches, no-force-kill behavior, rollback/reopen behavior, truthful copy, and macOS Apple-Silicon plus Windows compilation without packaging.

requirements.statement: Package the RU-065 verified client, including the Settings account-boundary cleanup, as distinct 0.4.12 internal installers for universal macOS and Windows x64 without publishing or enabling automatic updates.
acceptance: package.json, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and tauri.conf.json identify this candidate as 0.4.12, while the existing 0.4.11 artifacts remain unchanged and distinguishable.

The complete current renderer and native suites, TypeScript check, formatting, strict Rust lint, production renderer build, Apple-Silicon compilation and Windows x64 compilation pass before artifact acceptance.

The macOS DMG contains a universal x86_64 and arm64 app, uses the installed Developer ID identity with hardened runtime, receives accepted Apple notarization tickets for the app and DMG, is stapled, and passes codesign, Gatekeeper, stapler, architecture, bundle-version and disk-image verification.

The Windows payload is freshly cross-built for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and packaged by the SHA-256 pinned makensis 3.12 bottle with a closed Simplified-Chinese current-user NSIS recipe, shortcuts, normal-close request and uninstall registration.
The Windows artifact is explicitly recorded as unsigned, cross-built and not installed on a real Windows device; it does not claim Authenticode, SmartScreen reputation or bundled WebView2 coverage.

A machine-readable receipt binds the current source-state hash, RU-061 cross-platform verification, RU-065 Settings verification, test counts, tool hashes and artifact hashes. No tag, GitHub Release, upload, updater artifact, update manifest, server, NewAPI, database or user configuration change occurs.

requirements.statement: Correct the broken 0.4.12 Windows package so a release build always embeds the renderer instead of loading the development server, and ensure a Windows user can safely exit even when the renderer is unavailable, then produce a distinct local 0.4.13 Windows x64 repair installer.
acceptance: Cargo defines custom-protocol as the default production feature and a release-only compile guard rejects any build that omits the embedded frontend, while Tauri development continues to opt out through its observed --no-default-features command.

The Windows close button uses a native three-way choice that can completely exit, minimize to background or cancel without requiring renderer JavaScript; native exit requests start the same cooperative runtime shutdown path.

The corrected x86_64 Windows executable contains both current renderer asset paths and an embedded-custom-protocol runtime marker, contains no dev-server runtime marker, and is different from the rejected 0.4.12 payload.

The current renderer and native suites, typecheck, format, strict lint, production renderer build and Windows x64 compile pass before the distinct 0.4.13 Simplified-Chinese current-user NSIS installer is accepted.

The receipt explicitly supersedes only the 0.4.12 Windows artifact and retains unsigned, cross-built and not-yet-real-Windows-smoke-tested limits. No macOS rebuild, upload, updater publication, server, NewAPI, database or user configuration mutation occurs.

invariants: An account session is never projected into a third-party tool configuration.
Client cost calculations are estimates; the server billing ledger is authoritative.
V1 observes but does not install, update, or uninstall third-party AI tools.
A desktop application observation is separate from a command-line executable observation and cannot prove login, configuration or end-to-end compatibility.
A diagnostic conclusion names only causes supported by collected evidence.

A configuration write cannot commit without a recovery snapshot and external-change check. DEC-078 authorizes one encrypted pre-connection baseline per tool until explicit restoration; no backup history.

contracts.authorization: Bundled local desktop webview commands only. The native owner accepts only one compiled line ID and never returns a device code, access token, refresh token, session ID, tool token or local path to the renderer.
contracts.idempotency: Inspect and refresh are newest-request projections. One stored desktop session is reusable on either compiled first-party origin. Only confirmed authentication failure, expiry, explicit logout or revocation clears the credential.
contracts.compatibility: IPC5 adds sanitized money and recent savings aggregates. Legacy3/4 remain readable without inventing monetary basis. Commands, auth and optional billing semantics stay unchanged.

contracts.compatibility: Retain wire schema 1 and command name; accept all seven compiled tools. Desktop targets use structured platform activation; DSH reuses its managed browser process.

Opening CLI terminal is an explicit user action, not a paid probe or proof of response. Validate owned settings and active credential read-only before launching; caller never supplies command, path or URL.

contracts.authorization: One explicit click in the bundled desktop shell while a valid first-party desktop session exists. Native code accepts only two compiled active line IDs, seven closed target IDs, exact current-account model/group bindings and an optional native installation handoff. restartRunningApp is accepted only for Claude Desktop or Codex Desktop after the renderer shows an explicit save-work confirmation; it authorizes a normal quit request and reopen, never force termination. Keys remain native.
contracts.idempotency: Repeated activation reuses the target dedicated NewAPI token and replaces only receipt-owned fields. A same-tool pending encrypted transaction is recovered first; completed records are never auto-restored. A running desktop app returns application_running before account, key or file mutation unless the confirmed restart flag is present. Configuration ready is recomputed from atomic write/readback and local runtime readiness, not a paid model reply.
contracts.compatibility: Wire schema remains version 4. The optional restartRunningApp boolean defaults false and application_running is a new closed outcome. Existing model catalogs, exact model/group routing, connection receipts and first-request diagnostics remain compatible. CLI tools keep current sessions untouched and take effect in a new session; Claude Desktop and Codex Desktop may be normally quit and reopened after explicit confirmation.

errorSemantics: Invalid target, active line, model, billing group, installation identity or restart flag fails before key acquisition or file access.

A synchronous ready result requires the target credential in native secure storage, atomic configuration commit with semantic readback, the required helper-owned loopback runtime listening, and an applicable desktop or DSH open dispatch. It never waits for or bills an upstream model request.

Claude Desktop and Codex Desktop are checked again under the activation lock. If running and restartRunningApp is absent, application_running returns before mutation. With explicit consent native code requests a normal quit, waits only for a bounded exit, never force-terminates, and reopens only the exact discovered target.

A refused or incomplete normal quit leaves settings untouched and returns application_running with graceful_restart_required. CLI tools never terminate an existing terminal or editor session; their new configuration applies to a new session. Only helper-owned runtimes may be restarted.

Configuration, secure-storage, local-runtime and launch failures remain distinct closed outcomes. A failing local transaction restores touched files and prior credentials and deletes only a newly created token whose ownership is proven; a desktop app normally closed for the attempt is reopened against restored settings.

After ready, the first real application request is observed by the existing local gateway and exposed through recent connection results. An upstream timeout, quota, model or provider error does not roll back a configuration that was already atomically installed.
Complete keys never cross renderer IPC, appear in ordinary configuration or enter diagnostic text. Loopback compatibility endpoints return only public model metadata and health state.
Duplicate or unregistered model/group is rejected; no implicit default/group substitution. Cancellation before local write is safe; after write must restore locally or retain recovery state.

An installer handoff atomically consumes its one-use intent before credential or configuration work, checks full selection and exact installed target, and uses the captured native epoch throughout existing session-guarded activation.

A same-tool pending recovery record is self-healed only on a new explicit activation under the cross-process lock; incomplete file, credential or receipt cleanup remains non-ready with manual restore fallback.

Claude Desktop aliases are accepted only when derived from the current credential model set and resolve to exactly one real model, group and key before dispatch; Claude Code behavesAs never replaces the transmitted model ID.

default.behavior: Show the 野菜API welcome shell, the fixed five-tool list, and one primary button labelled to check installed tools.

default.recovery: The user may start the local scan or close the app without changing the machine.
default.correlation: A requestId is generated only when the user starts a scan.

loading.behavior: Keep all five tool cards visible with per-tool checking indicators and disable duplicate scan submission while the current request is active.
loading.visibleTruth: The page says that local executables and their version output are being checked and that no configuration or network action is running.
prohibitedClaims: Do not show cached installation or compatibility results as the active scan result.
loading.freshness: The active requestId and start time own the pending result.
loading.recovery: If the request fails, transition to error while retaining no invented tool status.
loading.correlation: Only the active requestId may complete this state.

empty.behavior: Show all five tools as not found and explain that this is not an application error.
empty.visibleTruth: The most recent completed local scan found no executable candidate for any supported tool.
prohibitedClaims: Do not claim the tools are uninstalled when they may exist outside the bounded discovery locations.
empty.freshness: Show the completion time of the newest accepted requestId.
empty.recovery: The user may install a tool independently and rescan; RU-001 never installs it.

partial.behavior: Show each of the five tool results independently so found, not-found, failed, timed-out, and read-only states can coexist.
partial.visibleTruth: Only observations from the newest completed local scan appear, including exact version text for successful probes.
prohibitedClaims: Do not promote one tool's success into a claim about another tool or about configuration health.

error.behavior: Show a plain-language scan failure without replacing it with guessed installation results.
error.visibleTruth: The discovery query did not produce a valid complete five-tool projection.
prohibitedClaims: Do not display the previous scan as if it were the failed request's current result.
error.freshness: The failed requestId is identified and prior results are visibly stale or cleared.
error.recovery: Retry creates a new requestId and performs the same bounded read-only scan.
error.correlation: The safe local error class is correlated to the failed requestId; raw command output is not displayed.

expired.behavior: Mark a superseded result as expired and prevent it from overwriting a newer request.

recovery.correlation: The recovery request receives its own requestId.

processing.behavior: Represent each bounded version probe as in progress while keeping configuration and remote-service controls absent.

processing.recovery: Each probe times out into a truthful per-tool result; the overall projection still completes when possible.
processing.correlation: Per-tool processing is aggregated under one requestId without persistent telemetry.

Fresh renderer-embedded Windows x64 payload and Simplified-Chinese current-user NSIS installer
Machine-readable regression, source, tool and artifact receipt
Human-readable 0.4.12 rejection and 0.4.13 Windows test handoff

migrationPolicy.dataBackfill: No local data, account, credential, configuration or database migration. Installing 0.4.13 replaces only the current-user executable through the existing installer identity.
migrationPolicy.rollback: Retain 0.4.12 evidence but do not distribute its Windows executable. If a gate fails, discard only unshipped 0.4.13 files and make no user or remote mutation.

compatibilityPolicy.strategy: Preserve desktop-account-session@v5, desktop-tool-activation@v10, desktop-open-connection@v2 and desktop-connection-management@v2. Change only shell production-mode selection, Windows close presentation and release identity.
compatibilityPolicy.supportedVersions: Internal repair candidate for Windows 10 22H2 and Windows 11 x64 with an existing WebView2 Runtime. Real-device validation remains required before public distribution.
compatibilityPolicy.removalGate: Do not use or publish the 0.4.12 Windows package. Do not call 0.4.13 Windows-ready until the owner confirms a real-device launch, visible bundled UI and complete exit.

requiredAcceptanceScenarios.assertion: Source and cross-platform compilation prove release builds cannot omit custom-protocol and Windows close or native quit can reach cooperative shutdown without renderer JavaScript.

The distinct 0.4.13 Windows x64 payload contains the current renderer asset paths and embedded runtime marker, excludes the dev-server marker, differs from 0.4.12 and is packaged by the closed Chinese NSIS recipe with truthful limits.
